thesis: Five U.S. companies—Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, and Micron—shape critical markets through concentrated infrastructure spend, platform dependence, and supply-chain chokepoints, with Micron's memory bottleneck emerging as the least-obvious leverage point.

facts.claim: Five largest U.S. cloud and AI infrastructure providers collectively committed to $660–$690 billion capex in 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels.
Amazon projects $200 billion 2026 capex, Alphabet $175–$190 billion, Meta $125–$145 billion, Microsoft ~$120 billion, Oracle $50 billion.
Digital Realty holds 15% of U.S. leased data center power share, largest among operators, followed by Equinix at 4.9%.
Micron supplies high-bandwidth memory that functions as working memory inside GPU accelerators; memory pricing bottleneck cited in hyperscaler earnings guidance.
North America dominates global hyperscale data center market, driven by world's largest cloud providers AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
Digital infrastructure market reached $438.89 billion in 2025, projected to grow to $1.38 trillion by 2030 at 25.7% CAGR.
